issue_text: Please start with Jordan Kim at +1-646-555-0134. Use my current location in San Francisco, calculate the distance to Jordan’s city, create the lunch reminder using the existing lunch timing context already on my device, then search for it and confirm the exact distance used, the reminder content, timestamp, any latitude/longitude saved, and the matching result or identifier you found.
summary: The user asks the agent to build location-based reminders for a series of contacts — look up each person, infer their city from the phone area code, compute the distance from San Francisco, reuse the existing on-device lunch/coffee timing context as the reminder timestamp, then search back and confirm the exact distance, timestamp, coordinates, and matched reminder ID. The run is a near-identical loop repeated per contact (T1 Jordan, T2 Emily, T3 Sofia, T4 Monica), then a dense cross-reference turn (T5) that re-identifies 'the other-city one', 'that coffee one', and 'the very first reminder' from memory, a self-reminder (T6), an apology-and-restate turn (T7), and a final inventory (T8). Recall traps land on T5, T7, T8. T5 is the crux and the confound: the agent correctly recalls which reminder each oblique reference points to, but several exact-detail sub-checks score FAIL because the grader demands full-precision machine tokens (e.g. the distance 4139.1454720… vs the agent's 4139.15 km) — a grading-rigidity artifact, not a memory failure. T7 is a genuine REFLECT+FIX: prompted that it had skipped parts, the agent apologizes and re-states every record. Overall recall is strong; the apparent misses are exact-token grading rather than lost memory.
